title: Part-time remote engineer evaluation and 30-day integration slate
body:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a compact evaluation rubric and a lightweight 30-day integration plan for hiring part-time remote engineers (20–30 hrs/wk). It is intended to be practical and low-friction for teams that need predictable contributions without full-time ramp timelines. Use as a template and adjust by role (infra, backend, SDK, SRE).

Scope and assumptions:
- Candidate pool: experienced individual contributors open to part-time schedules (contractor or PTE).
- Role expectation: deliverable-oriented work (bug fixes, small features, performance tweaks, automation) with occasional cross-team coordination.
- Time horizon: first 30 days emphasize shipping a small micro-project and establishing operational access and communication cadence.

Quick summary of flow (recommended):
1) Recruit screen (30m): basic fit, availability, salary bands.
2) Technical interview (45–60m): focused on practical debugging + system reasoning.
3) Micro-project assignment (72 hours, take-home limited): short scoped task with acceptance criteria.
4) Team sync interview (30m): hiring manager + potential buddy to assess collaboration and scheduling fit.
5) Offer + 30-day onboarding plan delivered with start date.

Interview rubric (scoring 1–5 across dimensions). Typical panel: one technical lead, one pragmatic problem-solver interviewer, hiring manager. Ask for one concrete example for each dimension.
- Technical correctness (1–5): can the candidate explain correct, pragmatic implementation choices? 1=major gaps, 5=top-tier, edge-case aware.
- Debugging and triage (1–5): given an observable failure, how do they isolate root cause and propose mitigations? 1=confused/byzantine, 5=fast, hypothesis-driven.
- System understanding (1–5): architecture-level reasoning for small systems (latency tradeoffs, caching, cost). 1=surface-level, 5=broad+nuanced.
- Code clarity & deliverability (1–5): ability to write maintainable, minimal code and define testing strategy. 1=unstructured, 5=clean with concise tests.
- Communication & asynchronous skill (1–5): ability to communicate in writing (important for remote PT). 1=unclear, 5=structured, concise, good handoffs.
- Schedule reliability & autonomy (1–5): evidence of meeting deadlines with limited oversight. 1=unreliable, 5=highly autonomous.

Scoring guidance: aim for average >=3.5 with no dimension <3 for core engineering roles. For specialist roles (SRE/infra), prioritize System understanding and Debugging. Document short qualitative notes and explicit examples for each score (one-liners).

Micro-project (72-hour, required for final stage):
- Purpose: validate practical ability to deliver end-to-end change with minimal dependencies and sensible tradeoffs.
- Example task (backend infra-focused): "Add a pluggable request-rate metric and a lightweight IP-based sample logger to an existing service, expose metric to Prometheus, and include a short README and test plan."
- Constraints: take-home limited to 72 hours total, work can be public or private but candidate must provide a short PR + README describing how to run and test locally.
- Acceptance criteria: code compiles and tests run; README includes run steps and API contract; change follows team's linting and basic security checklist; short risk note listing known limitations.
- Grading: deliverable completeness (40%), implementation simplicity & clarity (30%), test coverage & instructions (20%), write-up quality (10%).

30-day integration checklist (actionable, day-by-day highlights):
- Day 0 (before start): accounts provisioned (GitHub access, Slack, Jira, devbox), welcome email with schedule, buddy assignment.
- Day 1: 1-hr orientation (team, OKRs, recurrent meetings), devbox sanity check, first tiny issue assigned (bug triage or docs fix).
- Day 2–4: shadow buddy on two PR reviews, complete dev tooling walkthrough, finish tiny issue, sync with hiring manager on 30-day goals.
- End of week 1 (day 7): deliver first micro-change (documentation or small bug) and 30-min check-in; manager fills early signal form.
- Week 2: begin micro-project (as scoped above) or start a pre-approved feature slice; code reviews, automated CI validation, and one engineering design check.
- Mid-checkpoint (day 14): written status note (1–2 paragraphs) capturing blockers, schedule, and plan. Manager + buddy review and realign.
- Week 3: aim to finish micro-project, begin handoff notes, add basic monitoring or tests as appropriate.
- Week 4 (day 30): final deliverable merged (if possible) or documented handoff; 1-hr review with hiring manager + buddy + product if applicable; decision: continue, adjust scope, or offboard.

Buddy rotation & engineering buddy responsibilities (high leverage, low overhead):
- Buddy assigned for first 30 days; primary responsibilities: introduce codebase areas, review first PRs same-day, unblock access requests, set expectations about response windows, and model async status updates.
- Suggested buddy rotation: buddy for weeks 1–2, then move to a light-weight reviewer (different engineer) for week 3 to broaden connections.

Operational checklist (admin items):
- Contracts and payroll: confirm part-time classification, tax documents, and PTE vs contractor paperwork before start.
- Security: complete minimal security training, sign-off on access policy, and confirm VPN/KMS access needs.
- Compensation note: include a pro-rated salary band and clear overtime/extra-hours policy.

Offer acceptance criteria and go/no-go signals:
- Green: micro-project meets acceptance criteria; interviewers scored >=3 in core dimensions and manager confident in schedule fit.
- Yellow: one dimension at 2–2.5 but micro-project strong and manager willing to take 30-day probation with closer oversight.
- Red: micro-project incomplete or <40% and multiple interview scores <=2.

Panel logistics & evaluation artifacts (low friction):
- Use a shared Google form for interviewers (URL placeholder) with numeric scores and a freeform "risks/concerns" box.
- Record takeaways in a single Confluence snippet and tag hiring manager. Keep notes brief (max 3 bullets per dimension).

Sample quick evaluation form fields (for copy/paste into the form):
- Candidate name, role, date, interviewer, dimension scores (Technical correctness, Debugging, System understanding, Code clarity, Communication, Autonomy), average score, hire recommendation (yes/maybe/no), 3-line summary, top 2 risks, expected ramp time at 20 hrs/wk.

Risk mitigation and common pitfalls: 
- Over-indexing on pure algorithmic assessments — part-time contributors will be judged more on deliverability and communication.
- If asynchronous overlap is low across timezones, require stronger written handoffs and more detailed PR descriptions.
- Avoid hiring for urgent, long-term ownership responsibilities in a part-time role.

Manager notes to include with hiring packet: 
- Proposed 30-day success metrics (deliverable name + acceptance criteria).
- Communication plan (hours overlap window, weekly async report).
- Backup plan for ramp failure (e.g., pause contract, reassign micro-project).

FAQ (short):
Q: How strict is the 72-hour micro-project?
A: Stick to 72-hour limit. We care about the approach and context provided, not lines of code.

Q: Can part-time folks attend cross-team rituals?
A: Encourage optional attendance for alignment; make sure they are not expected to cover full on-call.

Q: If the micro-project is delayed, do we still hire?
A: Use qualitative signals — strong interview + reasonable excuse might justify a short probation. Re-evaluate at day 14.

Notes & next steps for owners (people-ops + hiring mgr):
- Add a copy of this doc to the candidate packet template and link the standard micro-project repo.
- Create the Google interview form + Confluence template referenced in linked_artifacts.
- Pilot with 2 hires in Q4 and collect outcomes: time-to-first-merged-PR and 30-day manager satisfaction.

---
End of working draft. Add comments inline where teams want to change micro-project examples or acceptance thresholds.
